geometry_edits.rationale: Shift the protected hall macro to a monitor roof family to express span and daylight, which is required for gymnasium section logic.
Keep the hall roof spanning along the x-axis so the long-span reading remains legible in section.
Replace the radial array with a stacked relation to reduce collision and recover a clearer hall/support hierarchy.
Limit the stack to two parts: hall and support.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the radial repetition that is producing collision-prone faceting with a simpler stacked mass relation more appropriate to a gymnasium hall and service hierarchy.
Reduce the fragment count to preserve one dominant hall and one subordinate support element.
Keep only a slight bend/offset so the silhouette stays continuous instead of reading as a star-like collision.
Change the hall section toward a monitor/daylight logic instead of an arbitrary cascading roof profile.
Align the long-span hall logic with the existing linear datum so the roof section reinforces the primary hall rather than fighting it.

rationale: The massing is readable as an hourglass-like, heavily faceted object with some internal axial continuity, but it does not convincingly resolve into the required gymnasium contract. Across views the form appears pinched and self-colliding in the middle, with the top/bottom widening but no clear long-span hall volume or subordinate service bar. The section is especially weak for a gymnasium: the roof expression reads as an arbitrary stepped/radial deformation rather than a span- or daylight-driven hall roof. There is also essentially no public void or ground carve responding to access. The result is more sculptural than programmatic, and the visible geometry does not yet support a clear athletics hall with entry hierarchy.
